title: The Sensor That Hears Drones Without Radar
description: Engineers at Florida International University, Brookhaven National Laboratory and a Sri Lankan university built a passive sensor that detects small drones from the faint magnetic field their motors leak. It transmits nothing, works to about fifteen metres in outdoor tests, and the team says it costs a few hundred dollars to develop.

beats.vo: This sensor catches drones while sending nothing at all.

beats.name: Arjuna Madanayake
beats.vo: Professor Arjuna Madanayake leads the team at Florida International University, with Brookhaven National Laboratory and a Sri Lankan university. But here's the part nobody tells you: it has no radio at all.

beats.text: Drone motors leak a magnetic signature
beats.vo: A drone's brushless motors leak a faint magnetic field that pulses with their spin. A one metre loop antenna listens, and a neural network reads the pattern. Nothing is transmitted, so nothing gives the sensor away.

beats.text: Catch: range is about 15 metres, so it guards a spot.
beats.vo: The catch: range is about fifteen metres outdoors, so it guards one spot, not a city. Detection hit ninety eight point five percent, but telling three drone models apart was lower.
Know someone who thinks radar is the only way? Send them this: a drone's own motors give it away.

caption:
A drone sensor that transmits nothing? Yes, and it's real. 📡
FIU engineers detect small drones from the magnetic field their motors leak: loop antenna, neural network, a few hundred dollars to develop.
The catch: about 15 m range outdoors, 98.5% detection. Models were harder to tell apart.
